method_notes: All checks run from the Higgsfield sandbox (open internet) plus WebSearch. Licence tags re-read from raw README front matter AND the Hugging Face API (cardData.license) or Internet Archive /metadata API. Every media_url re-requested with curl -sIL (final status after redirects recorded). Every Rapidata mp4 and both FETV members were downloaded and re-probed (ffprobe), scanned for C2PA manifests (c2pa-python), scanned for scene cuts (ffmpeg scene>0.15), letterbox bars, static-overlay watermarks (temporal-std + edge analysis) and burnt-in text (RapidOCR on every 10th frame). Archive.org Karpathy/Izdepski/Cole items sampled with ffmpeg over HTTP and OCR'd. NO frame was viewed by a human or a vision model: 'no watermark found' means no static overlay and no OCR text in sampled frames, not a visual all-clear. Higgsfield video_analysis jobs queued by H6 were still 'queued' (not started) when checked, so they were not used.
cross_cutting_findings: RAPIDATA LICENCE EVIDENCE (applies to 11 candidates): the only licence text is the dataset-card front matter 'license: apache-2.0' (confirmed in raw README and API cardData for Rapidata/text-2-video-human-preferences, -veo2, -veo3, -veo3.1, -wan2.1, -seedance-1-pro, -moonvalley-marey). The cards never say who generated the videos, never say the licence covers the mp4 files, and never mention upstream model terms. Apache-2.0 is a software licence (licence-copy/notice duties). The hunter's statement that 'Rapidata generated the video itself' is an inference, not written on any card; the benchmark methodology page (benchmark.ai/methodology) only says 'a pairing of generated outputs from two models'. Card metadata is also sloppy (the -veo3 repo's pretty_name is 'Pika 2.2 Human Preferences'; the -veo2 and -wan2.1 dataset_info blocks are byte-identical). Recommended for every Rapidata clip: obtain a one-line written confirmation from Rapidata that they generated the clip, hold the rights to license it, and that the generating account/plan permitted commercial use.

UPSTREAM TERMS: read and OK for Google (Gemini API terms: 'Google won't claim ownership over that content.'), OpenAI (Wayback 2024-12-09 terms: 'you (a) retain your ownership rights in Input and (b) own the Output. We hereby assign to you all our right, title, and interest'), Runway (current terms: 'does not claim ownership of any of your Inputs or Outputs... does not restrict your commercial use of your Outputs' - 2026 text, not the Jan-2025 text), Alibaba Wan2.1 (Apache-2.0; 'We claim no rights over the your generated contents'). CONDITIONAL: Luma ('can only use the Outputs for commercial purposes if the Outputs were produced during an active Subscription Term under Customer's paid subscription') and Pika ('personal, noncommercial use only' unless the Plan expressly permits commercial use) - Rapidata's plan unknown. NOT READ (JS shells): Kling, ByteDance Seedance/BytePlus. BLOCKING: Tencent Hunyuan (see reject).

MODEL PROVENANCE: only the Sora and Runway files carry C2PA manifests (independent of the dataset labels). Veo 2 and Veo 3.1 files carry container tag encoder=Google. Wan 2.1 (832x480, 81 frames, 16 fps) and Hunyuan (129 frames, 24 fps) match their published default settings. All other model labels rest solely on Rapidata's file names / parquet 'model' column / README (verified internally consistent: parquet file_name -> model -> prompt matches the candidate for all 11).

CROWD-RANK CLAIMS VERIFIED: Rapidata/1k-ranked-videos-coherence parquet (1,026 rows) - top Elo: hunyuan_0082_421 1645, wan2.1_0066_0 1639, pika_0006_1718154969 1621, sora_0048_1 1608 (tie with pika2.2_0005_1); lowest Elo: ray2_0094_1 757; alpha_0066_690998814 1584; veo2_0094_0 874. README: question was 'Which video has more glitches and is more likely to be AI-generated?' and 'a higher Elo score indicates worse performance'. Any caption must say 'ranked among the most glitch-flagged of 1,026 sampled clips in Rapidata's benchmark' and must not imply the clip represents the model's typical output.
SAMPLING BIAS: every 'failure' clip is the worst of its model, every 'best' clip is the best; brief rule 'nothing may imply curated demos represent every generation' applies to both ends.

issues_found: BLOCKING upstream encumbrance missed by the hunter: Tencent Hunyuan Community Licence (raw LICENSE.txt, 'Release Date: December 3, 2024') opens 'THIS LICENSE AGREEMENT DOES NOT APPLY IN THE EUROPEAN UNION, UNITED KINGDOM AND SOUTH KOREA' and section 5(c) says 'You must not use, reproduce, modify, distribute, or display the Tencent Hunyuan Works, Output or results of the Tencent Hunyuan Works outside the Territory. Any such use outside the Territory is unlicensed and unauthorized under this Agreement.' The hunter summarised this as 'does not treat Output as a licensed Work' - that understates it: the licence expressly restricts DISPLAY/DISTRIBUTION OF OUTPUT outside the Territory. A public 120 s film cannot be geo-fenced away from the EU/UK. (Section 6(d) also says 'Tencent claims no rights in Outputs You generate', so the practical risk may be low, but it is an unresolved contractual restriction and Rapidata's Apache-2.0 tag cannot remove it.)
Rapidata's Apache-2.0 card does not state that Rapidata generated the clip or that it may sublicense Tencent-model Output (see cross_cutting_findings).
Model sub-version unstated (README spells 'Hunyouan'; file name 'hunyuan'). Creation date is the HF upload date (2025-01-10), not the generation date.
